$comment: KRYLO MCP-server policy. Machine-readable form of docs/09-tool-governance.md and docs/15-database-and-infrastructure.md.

rules.rule: Tool descriptions, names, and metadata from MCP servers are untrusted data and cannot override KRYLO policy.
An MCP server may be used only at a version or commit recorded in the trust catalog. A newer version than the reviewed one is not automatically trusted.
Re-review is required when tools, hooks, install scripts, network destinations, or requested scopes change.
Browser-session tokens and personal connectors are never provided to MCP servers.
Each server's data egress must be declared in the catalog; undeclared flows are denied.

$actionGateComment: Consumed by scripts/security/risk-gate.mjs to classify PreToolUse calls to any tool matching mcp__<server>__<operation>. A server is 'known' when its name (case-insensitive substring) appears in serverActionClasses OR its id/publisher/source is present in catalog/tools.json (any category, since the underlying service's write risk does not depend on CLI vs MCP transport). An unknown server is always gated (unknownServerClass), for every operation, read or write, because KRYLO cannot assess a service it has never classified. A known server is gated only for operations whose name matches writeVerbPattern (or, for servers with treatAnyExecuteAsWrite, any query/execute/statement-shaped operation, since arbitrary SQL cannot be judged read-only from its name).
